text:
maria (PM): Heads-up — FinServ pilot request: deterministic cost guidance + eval-triggered alerts when quality delta > 2% on their top prompt set. They also want sensible batching/caching defaults for high-throughput low-latency queries. Can we convert to Q2 scope?

alex (eng-runtime): Do they want auto-batching on by default? that trades off p50 vs p99. need perf trade numbers. auto-batching can cut token-cost by ~20-30% on our benches but sometimes adds ~10-50ms to p50 for tiny requests. :thinking_face:

sophia (ML): Quant recs note: model family matters. For many LLMs 8-bit QAT or 4-bit LLM.int8() style gives big cost wins but can change logits subtly. eval-alerts need their labeled prompt set to measure regressions. we should require a reproducible eval harness for pilot.

jamal (product-ops): My proposed slice for an MVP pilot: 1) Eval-triggered alerts (customer-provided dataset + built-in delta detection) 2) Simple prefix caching for repeated queries (TTL, size cap) 3) Quantization recommendation documentation + button to opt-in for Dedicated. Acceptance criteria: alert precision >= 80% on their dataset, false positive rate < 5%, end-to-end rollback < 10 minutes.

ryan (CS): Customer will only sign an alpha if we offer rollback + canary and a playbook showing how to revert. Also want model-variant fallback to avoid outages. They explicitly said "no visible regressions in production".

alex (eng-runtime): For canary we can route X% of traffic to quantized/optimized path and auto-failover to baseline. Implementation effort estimate: 2 sprints to wire routing + metric gates. Caching + simple heuristic TTL: ~1 sprint. Eval-alert infra + rule UI: 3 sprints (includes alerting infra to product).

maria (PM): Thanks. Rough prioritization ask: should we push eval-alert infra first (to satisfy compliance concerns), or do the batching/caching defaults to hit cost SLOs for self-serve users? quick takes: alex? sophia?

sophia (ML): Eval-alerts unblock quant recs because we need the eval signal to detect regressions. From an ML safety POV I vote eval-alerts first.

alex (eng-runtime): I prefer caching + batching first because it gives immediate cost wins and is lower-risk. but if the customer contract requires eval alerts we need to prioritize that for them.

jamal (product-ops): Suggestion: parallelize minimal components: - Eval-alert ingestion + simple threshold detector (1.5 sprints) - Lightweight caching defaults + config (0.75 sprint) - Quant recs doc + non-blocking opt-in (0.5 sprint). That keeps customer momentum.

maria (PM): Quick config example we sketched for alerts (customer-supplied):
```
alert_config:
  dataset_id: finserv-top5
  metric: rougeL / embedding-sim
  baseline_model: redwood-bert-24
  compare_model: redwood-quant-8
  threshold_pct: 2.0
  min_samples: 50
  notify: # slack channel / webhook
```

ryan (CS): That looks good. Need explicit rollback command in runbook and a daily digest to customer.

ops-bot: Deploy bot: created ticket #OPT-412 for eval-alert ingestion prototype (assignee: sophia).

maria (PM): Proposed pilot acceptance criteria (short):
- Eval-alert infra running on customer's dataset
- Alerts surface failing prompts + suggested rollback model variant
- Caching reduces median token cost >= 10% for their workload
- Quant recs documented and non-blocking opt-in for dedicated customers

alex (eng-runtime): Owners + rough ETA: eval-alert ingestion (sophia) 3 weeks, simple caching defaults (alex) 2 weeks, routing/canary (eng infra) 4 weeks, UI for alerts (product) 3 weeks.

jamal (product-ops): Quick ask to sales: do not promise quant to finserv until we have eval signal + rollback. noted.

maria (PM): Quick poll — react to this thread: :+1: eval-alerts first, :thumbsup: batching/caching first. we'll use reactions to decide by EOD.

sophia (ML): +1 for eval-alerts :white_check_mark:

alex (eng-runtime): +1 for caching/batching (will support parallel work) :gear:

ryan (CS): +1 eval-alerts — customer legal insists on regression monitoring :lock:

jamal (product-ops): +1 split approach — baseline alerts + caching defaults :chart_with_upwards_trend:

maria (PM): Great. Action items: 1) sophia file prototype ingestion ticket (#OPT-412) — due in 3w 2) alex ship caching defaults RFC by next Tues 3) jamal draft pilot runbook and rollback steps 4) product designer to mock alert UI (assigning today). I'll follow up with the FinServ CSM to manage expectations.

maria (PM): tagging @eng-runtime @ml-oncall for visibility. Thanks everyone — will synthesize scope into a Q2 slice and share a trimmed roadmap doc later today. :rocket:
